items.title: Myra Menville Interview, 1958-05-07, 09
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Maybe like Papa Salister? [INTERVIEWEE] No, he was still playing, but he played any number of concerts for us.

ctx.x: No, that was organized in the early 40s. Oh. Then in 1948, when New Orleans Jazz Club came into being, and we've been going 10 years now. We've had some very fine concerts, and I really, without patting ourselves on the back, believe that two-thirds of the old musicians that are playing again today are due to our efforts of taking them up.

No, he was still playing, but he played any number of concerts for us. And Eddie Pearson's group, Paul Barbarine's group, George Lewis's group. That's talking about nothing with the Negroes. Shock, it was Steve Adorn on the room in front. And we dug him up. And Harry Shields, who was Larry's brother, he was running a diesel engine at night on a switch engine, LNN, and so on down the line, one after the other like that. And we just finally get together and play and jam, bring him up to the club, and finally we…
